subject: Emergency: temporary subprocessor switchover request (FinVault)
messages:
From: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@finvault.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: Emergency: temporary subprocessor switchover request

Michael —

Apologies for the early message. Our primary logging processor for the east region (third-party) has a datacenter-level outage and their recovery ETA is looking like >72h. We need to temporarily re-route a subset of ingestion (audit logs and non-PII telemetry) to an alternate processor for continuity.

Can Redwood support a temporary subprocessor switchover for the following scopes:
- Inbound audit logs (retention 30 days)
- Non-PII telemetry used for routing and monitoring

We need:
1) a short written confirmation that Redwood can accept a temporary processor swap for up to 7 days without amending the main DPA (we can sign an addendum)
2) evidence packet for the temporary processor (SOC2 Type II summary, encryption at rest description, country of processing)
3) an estimate of time to onboard and any expected changes to data residency or transfer paths

I've attached our high-level switch plan (finvault-temp-switchover-plan.pdf) and a proposed DPA addendum we can initial (dpa-addendum-draft.docx).

Thanks — we need to move fast. cc: Aaron Patel (security).

— Lina
Security Programs, FinVault
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@finvault.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Emergency: temporary subprocessor switchover request

Team — forwarding an urgent ask from FinVault. Key points: temporary processor for audit logs + non-PII telemetry, 7-day window, need SOC2 summary and residency. They attached a switchover plan and a draft DPA addendum.

Questions for legal/security:
- Can we accept a short-term subprocessor swap under our current DPA with a signed addendum?
- What minimum evidence do we require from the alternate processor (SOC2/ISO, KMS, access controls, personnel screening)?
- Any red flags around routing telemetry outside the US for this customer?

I'm happy to coordinate signatures and get a canary routing policy in place if we greenlight.

Attachments: finvault-temp-switchover-plan.pdf (plan), dpa-addendum-draft.docx (customer draft).

—Michael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@finvault.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Emergency: temporary subprocessor switchover request

Michael / Kim —

High-level security assessment notes:
- For non-PII telemetry + audit logs, a temporary processor is acceptable provided we obtain:
  * Current SOC2 Type II report (or summary bridge letter)
  * Confirmation of encryption at rest (algorithm + KMS ownership)
  * Minimal personnel access and role-based access controls (RBAC) description
  * Data routing map showing where logs will traverse (any EU hops must be flagged)

- Operational: we should limit retention to 30 days as the customer requests and avoid exporting PII. We'll add a canary routing rule to send <10% traffic initially and monitor errors and latency for 60 minutes before ramping.
- Compliance: if the alternate processor processes data in a non-US country we need to check their transfer mechanisms; for short-term emergency we can accept SCC-equivalent controls if legal signs off.

I can review their SOC2 summary when provided. From a timeline perspective, assuming documentation is in hand, engineering can implement canary routing within 3–5 hours and full switchover within 12–24 hours.

— Stephanie
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@finvault.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T15:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Emergency: temporary subprocessor switchover request

Lina —

Thanks for the heads-up and the draft. We can proceed on a temporary basis with an addendum; I attached a redlined DPA addendum with the minimum clauses I need (redlined-dpa.docx). Short summary of our requirements:

1) Scope & timebox: explicit 7-day maximum with an option to extend only by written mutual consent.
2) Evidence: SOC2 Type II or a certified summary; evidence of KMS controls + attestation that Redwood retains control of encryption keys (or equivalent segregation).
3) Access controls: least-privilege, MFA for all operator accounts, staff screening statement.
4) Data handling: no PII allowed to be routed; if any PII is present it must be isolated and not stored beyond 24 hours.
5) Indemnity & liability: limited to reasonable, commercially customary levels for a temporary workaround.

Operationally, we'll implement the canary as Stephanie suggested and will only flip the main route once security confirms the SOC2 summary and we have an executed addendum (DocuSign link would be preferred).

Next steps I propose:
- FinVault: share the SOC2 summary + KMS attestation for the alternate processor.
- Redwood (Kim / Steph): confirm canary parameters and deployment window (we can do an initial 10% ramp today at 18:30 PT).
- Michael: coordinate DocuSign for the attached redlined addendum.

If those items are delivered we can have the canary live within the day.

Best —
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined-dpa.docx (redlines and minimal clauses)
